title: Transmission representation of the Josephson free energy beyond the short-junction limit
abstract: Beenakker's formula, $U(\varphi)-U(0)=Δ\sum_n\bigl(1-\sqrt{1-τ_n\sin^2(\varphi/2)}\bigr)$, expresses the zero-temperature energy-phase relation of a short Josephson junction through its normal-state transmission eigenvalues. We generalize this transmission representation beyond the short-junction limit and express the phase-dependent free energy of a time-reversal-symmetric $s$-wave junction as a Matsubara sum over channels with frequency-dependent transmissions. The representation constrains the small-phase expansion of the free energy. In particular, we prove that the normalized ratio of its quartic and quadratic coefficients satisfies $-1\leα_r\le7/80$ at finite temperature. We also construct a four-site junction with $α_r>0$, which disproves the conjectured upper bound $α_r\le0$. So that these results can be trusted without repeating the derivations, every numbered equation is formally verified in the Lean proof assistant.
summary: This work extends the theoretical description of the Josephson free energy from the simple short-junction limit to arbitrary junction lengths. By using a generalized transmission representation derived from superconducting scattering theory, the authors derive strict mathematical bounds on the free energy's phase expansion coefficients. Crucially, they disprove a previous conjecture by constructing a physical counterexample, advancing the theoretical understanding of superconducting quantum junctions.
main_problem: The paper generalizes the transmission representation of the Josephson free energy beyond the standard short-junction limit.
main_result: It establishes new bounds on the ratio of quartic to quadratic coefficients ($\alpha_r$) and constructs a specific junction that disproves previous conjectures regarding the sign of this ratio.
method: The analysis uses Matsubara summation techniques applied to the determinant ratio derived from the Bogoliubov-de Gennes Hamiltonian, relating the free energy to channel-dependent transmissions.
model_or_system: The system is a time-reversal-symmetric s-wave Josephson junction (SNS junction). The analysis is performed using the BdG Hamiltonian and involves scattering theory techniques to derive the free energy difference.
key_observables: The phase-dependent free energy, $F_ eta(\varphi) - F_ eta(0)$, and the normalized ratio of its quartic and quadratic coefficients, $\alpha_r$.
important_parameters: Temperature ($ eta$), junction length (moving beyond the short-junction limit), and the superconducting gap ($\Delta$).
main_assumptions: The derivation assumes time-reversal symmetry and s-wave pairing. The results are rigorously verified using the Lean proof assistant.
figures_summary: Not specified, but the notes mention Figure 4 detailing the project's development timeline and prompt volume.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from the known short-junction limit (Beenakker's formula) to a generalized, finite-temperature, and finite-length transmission representation for the free energy. It then analyzes the resulting coefficients to derive rigorous bounds and provides a counterexample to existing conjectures.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical framework and the derivation of constraints on the free energy expansion coefficients are highly relevant to understanding non-equilibrium quantum dynamics and phase transitions in superconducting mesoscopic systems.
